### regional internet registries (RIRs)  {.smaller}

![map from Wikimedia Commons, users Dork, Canuckguy et al, Sénhur, CC-BY-SA 3.0](/arp/Regional_Internet_Registries_world_map.svg){fig-alt="Map of RIR areas of responsibilit; AFRNIC covers Africa; APNIC covers South and East Asia (excluding Russia) and Oceania; ARIN covers the United States and Canada; LACNIC covers Central and South America; RIPE NCC covers Greenland, Europe, the Middle East, and former USSR countries."}


* most useful addresses managed by RIRs 

   * African Network Information Centre (AFRINIC)
   * American Registry for Internet Numbers (ARIN)
   * Asia Pacific Network Information Centre (APNIC)
   * Latin American and Carribean Network Information Centre (LACNIC)
   * Réseaux IP Européens Network Coordination Centre (RIPE NCC)

### special IPv4 addresses 


[![](/arp/iana-special-ipv4-detail){fig-alt="Partial screenshot of special addresses on that pagei, each of which has a citation to an RFC. The address spaces include: 0/8 for 'this network', 0/32 for 'this host on this network', 10/8 for private use, 100.64/10 for shared address space, 127/8 for loopback, 192/24 for IETF protocol assignments, and more."}](https://www.iana.org/assignments/iana-ipv4-special-registry)


### selected special IP addresses  {.smaller}


* loopback (current machine) --- <code>127/8</code> (v4), <code>::1/128</code> (v6)
* link-local (current network only) --- 

   * <code>169.254/16</code> (v4), <code>ff80::/10</code> (v6)

* private use (non-public networks only) --- <br> 

   * <code>192.168/16</code>, <code>172.16/12</code>, <code>10/8</code> (v4), (kinda) <code>fc00::/7</code> (v6)

* multicast groups and related --- <code>224/4</code> (v4), <code>ff00::/8</code> (v6) 

   * multiple nodes can be part of a single ‘‘multicast group’’

* broadcast (all on current network) ---  

   * <code>255.255.255.255</code>, <code>ff01::1</code>

* ‘‘future use’’ ---  

   * rest of <code>240/4</code> (v4), <code>4000::</code>---<code>efff::</code> (v6)
